title: Upgrade app-lock verifiers to PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256
body:
## Summary

Affects `UtilFunctions.encodePbkdf2` in `app/src/main/java/app/michaelwuensch/bitbanana/util/UtilFunctions.java`.

I found that app-lock credentials are currently derived with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 at 5,000 iterations. This is below the PBEKeySpecSpec rule’s minimum of 10,000 iterations.

I added marked PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 verifiers with random salts and 100,000 iterations for new passwords and PINs. Existing SHA1/5,000 verifiers remain available for verification and are replaced only after successful authentication, preserving stored credentials and emergency-unlock behavior. I also clear locally created `PBEKeySpec` instances after derivation.

I found this while running the app under RVSec, a runtime-verification tool that watches the app's calls to the Java cryptography and TLS APIs and checks each sequence of calls against usage rules written in CrySL. `PBEKeySpecSpec` is the rule this code did not satisfy.

## How was this tested?

- No automated test was added in this change
- [x] Project compiles successfully (`assembleDebug`)
